surface_fix.what: refuse an id-less pre-field row when a fresher field-bearing capture refuses the same product under a longer name; and rule the harissa row known-wrong so the cell cannot come back through another path
surface_fix.exact_change: Get-ChannelVerdict: when -ItemId is blank and the capture is pre-field, look up the newest field-bearing row for the store whose normalized name StartsWith the id-less row's normalized name (require at least 40 chars, the truncated-key length class); if that row is FC or MARKETPLACE return in_store=$false with why='PRE-FIELD-NAMELESS-ROW-OUTLIVING-A-REFUSAL'. Then: add-known-wrong.ps1 -Commodity harissa-paste -Store Walmart -Name 'Mina Harissa Mild Sauce, Homestyle Moroccan Red Pepper Haris' -RuledBy triage-2026-09-02 -Evidence 'id-less 07-18 row of product 773599552, which the 08-31 capture marks FC (ship-only); a 46-day-old price of a product not sold in store held the crown at $0.845/oz'

items.root_cause: Two mechanisms. (a) price-history.json is written by update-history.ps1 (an idempotent per-week upsert) from check-ad-cycles in the MORNING chain and from weekly-post-capture only; the triage rebuild-and-republish path never calls it, so a board repaired in the afternoon leaves the morning's numbers in history and the next morning's sanity 'wow' compares today's correct cell against the superseded generation. Four of today's six flags (broccoli, harissa, insect-spray, jalapenos) are exactly that: every one carries an 08-31 history value the on-disk 08-31 board no longer holds. (b) The in-store channel gate can only propagate a refusal by item id; pre-field rows with no id are un-refusable, and the 48/61-char name truncation of that era means the refused product's full name never equals the id-less row's name, so the founding 'pre-field row outliving a refusal' fix cannot reach them. 24 Walmart cells (14 crowns) sit on that class; one of them is the harissa crown.

root_fix.what: make history follow the board it describes: the republish path upserts the board's week in price-history.json, so a rebuilt board corrects its own history row and the wow check compares like generations

items.root_cause: The include vocabulary encodes the STORE'S form words (mix, shredded, angel hair, tri-color) as if they were the product's, so a store that prints only 'Coleslaw' is invisible; and the one bare include ('cole slaw') has no deli fence, so ad copy that lists 'Potato Salad, Macaroni Salad or Cole Slaw' walks straight in. Same class as 'an each-commodity whose stores cannot all express a portion count': the rule depends on wording the store controls. Velveeta is the other half: the loosened coverage probe reads 'Block' as evidence and cannot tell a process cheese product from cheese.
items.root_fix_note: surface_fix IS the root fix for this commodity (form-agnostic include + deli fence). The class-level fix (a shared deli-salad token in GLOBAL_EXCLUDE) was NOT measured this round and is not proposed: 'potato salad' and 'macaroni salad' are themselves tracked elsewhere and a global token would blind them.

items.subject: Grocery: semantic sweep found 2 product(s) no rule can see - 2026-09-02
evidence: semantic-findings.json (08:15, cuda, board_pairs 3139, corpus 40958, rule_invisible 7479): ground-beef-8020 | Aldi | 'USDA 80% Lean 20% Fat Ground Beef Patties - 4 Count' (aldi-regular: 1.33 lb $6.64 = $4.99/lb) and '... - 10 Count', cos 0.7173 score 0.9055.

explain-coverage-gap.ps1 -Id ground-beef-8020 (run 11:58, rc 0): EXCLUDED x2 - include '80%?\s*lean[^.]*20%?\s*fat' matched, exclude 'patties' killed it. ground-beef-8020 [index 2] excludes: turkey || meatball || patty || patties || 93% ... - the refusal is deliberate and old.

Aldi is NOT missing from the commodity: aldi-regular holds 'Ground Beef 80 20 1 Per LB' $5.29/lb, '80 / 20 Ground Beef' 2.0 lb $12.38 and 'Family Pack 80 Lean 20 Fat Ground Beef Patties 2.5 LB' (also excluded). Patties are a formed product sold at a different price point ($4.99/lb vs $5.29/lb bulk here, usually dearer).

MEASURED, the pool the sweep draws from: of 10,934 corpus names no commodity claims, 6,924 (63%) are include-hit-then-excluded - deliberate refusals like this one - so 'no rule can see' is the wrong reading for most of the sweep's 7,479 rule-invisible names. The sweep does consult known-wrong.json (audit-semantic-identity.ps1 lines 135-137, 290), so a ruling is its designed terminal state.

surface_fix.what: rule both patty rows known-wrong for ground-beef-8020 @ Aldi so the sweep stops re-finding a product the exclude already refuses
surface_fix.exact_change: add-known-wrong.ps1 -Commodity ground-beef-8020 -Store Aldi -Name 'USDA 80% Lean 20% Fat Ground Beef Patties - 4 Count','USDA 80% Lean 20% Fat Ground Beef Patties - 10 Count' -RuledBy triage-2026-09-02 -Evidence 'formed patties, excluded by design (exclude patties); 80/20 bulk ground beef at Aldi is Ground Beef 80 20 1 Per LB $5.29'. No commodities.json change.

items.root_cause: The sweep labels every unclaimed name 'no rule can see' whether the engine never matched it or an exclude deliberately refused it; 63% of its pool is the second kind, so it will keep paging deliberate refusals (patties today, a pie-mix or a turkey twin tomorrow) until each gets a ruling. The explain step that separates NO-INCLUDE from EXCLUDED exists but runs only after the page.

root_fix.what: run the explain classification inside the sweep and say the class in the alert, so an EXCLUDED finding arrives as 'refused by exclude <x> - verify the exclude, else rule it' instead of 'no rule can see'
files: grocery/explain-coverage-gap.ps1 (expose its classifier as a function)
root_fix.exact_change: for each coverage finding, call the explain classifier (NO-INCLUDE / EXCLUDED / CLAIMED / MATCHES) and write it into semantic-findings.json as 'explain' plus the killing pattern; the alert body groups findings by class. Keep paging on all classes (an over-broad exclude is exactly what EXCLUDED can reveal - FF's 'deli'-killed cole slaw is one); only the WORDING and the recommended action change. No threshold moves.

(1) 'Member's Mark Broccoli Salad with Smoked Bacon, priced per pound' | Sam's | $5.85/lb, in every Sam's slice since 07-29 -> routes to bacon [4] (candidate broccoli [50]). Wrong owner both ways; today it loses the Sam's bacon cell on price only ('Member's Mark Restaurant Style Bacon, Hickory Smoked, 10lbs.' $3.784/lb). Two more deli salads ride bacon: Walmart 'Taylor Farms Caesar Salad with Bacon and Chicken, 5.75 oz' and 'Taylor Farms BLT Salad with Chicken and Bacon, 6.5 oz' ($3.47). Releasing bacon alone re-lands the broccoli salad on broccoli (second-order), so broccoli gets the same fence.

(2) 'Outshine Lime, Tangerine, and Lemon Frozen Fruit Pops, Variety Pack, 12 Count' | Baker's | $6.49 / 12 ct -> routes to frozen-fruit [273] (candidate popsicles [274], whose include literally has 'fruit\s+pops'). Wrong owner; not a cell (frozen-fruit is per oz, '12 ct' has no oz). Two sibling Outshine packs sit there too. lemons [45] and limes [46] are NOT in the contest: lemons excludes '\bfrozen\b' and the limes chain also refuses it (verified by the resolver: candidates = popsicles only).

(3) 'Quaker Dinosaur Eggs Brown Sugar Instant Oatmeal' | Baker's | $3.29 / 8 ct -> routes to EGGS [7] (candidate oatmeal [76]). Wrong owner; not a cell today (8 ct read as eggs = $4.94/dozen vs the Baker's cell 'Kroger Grade AA Large White Eggs' 60 ct $1.75/dozen) but it is one price move from being one.

(4) 'Southern Grove Dry Roasted Peanuts with Sea Salt' | Aldi ad | $2.29 / 16 oz -> routes to peanuts [226] (candidate sea-salt [591]). CORRECT owner. But the contest partner exposed a LIVE wrong crown-adjacent cell the soundness audit can never flag (only one include wants it, so it is not 'contested'): sea-salt @ Aldi = 'Southern Grove Deluxe Whole Cashews With Sea Salt 30 OZ' $10.49 / 30 oz = $0.3497/oz on the pinned board. Measured: 20 nut/candy/snack names route to sea-salt or salt today (Ghirardelli sea salt caramels at 4 stores, Member's Mark cashews/thins/caramels, Wonderful pistachios, Mauna Loa macadamias, Go Raw pumpkin seeds, RITZ Hint of Salt crackers, Simply Nature Sea Salt Pop Corn ...). Aldi's only true sea salt is 'Stonemill Sea Salt Grinder 3.53 OZ', already refused by the standing 'salt grinder' exclude.

ALSO MEASURED (same mechanism, garden seeds on produce, Walmart): 'Radish Vegetable Seeds 5 Pack' on radishes, 'Sprouting Seed Super Sampler ... 2.5 Lbs' $67.97 on broccoli (re-lands on dry-green-lentils once broccoli releases it), 'Red Russian Kale Seeds: 25 Lb' and a deer food-plot seed on kale, 'Utah Yellow Sweet Spanish Onion Garden Seeds - 5 Lb' on onions, 'Crisphead Lettuce Garden Seeds' on lettuce. None holds a cell today.

surface_fix.what: fence each of the four contests on the wrong side, narrow sea-salt to actual salt, rule the cashews known-wrong, and stop the seed packets
surface_fix.exact_change: bacon.exclude += '\bsalads?\b'; broccoli.exclude += '\bsalads?\b'; eggs.exclude += '\boatmeal\b', '\bdinosaur\b'; frozen-fruit.exclude += '\bpops?\b', '\bfruit\s+bars?\b'; sea-salt.include REPLACED by the single pattern recorded in the sidecar rule_changes (sea salt followed by a comma, a digit, end of string, an open paren, a hyphen, or one of: fine coarse kosher grinder shaker canister crystals flakes iodized mediterranean celtic pure natural); sea-salt.exclude += '\b(?:cashews?|almonds?|pistachios?|peanuts?|macadamia|nuts?|seeds?|caramels?|chocolate|thins|squares?|bars?)\b', '\bpop\s*corn\b', '\bstraws?\b', '\bedamame\b'; salt.exclude += '\b(?:pistachios?|crackers?)\b'; radishes.exclude += '\bseeds?\b', '\bsprouting\b'; compare-deals.ps1 GLOBAL_EXCLUDE += 'sprout(?:ing)?\s+seeds?'. Then add-known-wrong.ps1 -Commodity sea-salt -Store Aldi -Name 'Southern Grove Deluxe Whole Cashews With Sea Salt 30 OZ' -RuledBy triage-2026-09-02 -Evidence 'cashews priced as sea salt, $0.3497/oz, live cell on comparison-2026-09-02'.

items.root_cause: 'with <ingredient>' and '<ingredient> <snack>' flavour phrases route whole snack, candy and deli categories into staple commodities, and the soundness audit can only see the subset that TWO includes want (contested). A name only one include wants - the cashews on sea-salt - is never contested, passes every guard (real product, real price, plausible band) and becomes a cell. sea-salt's include '\bsea salt\b' is the worst case: at Aldi 19 rows contain 'sea salt' and exactly one is salt. Garden-seed packets are the produce twin of the same class (the vegetable's name is the seed's name).
items.root_fix_note: surface_fix IS the root fix for these commodities: the sea-salt include narrowing (form-word lookahead) replaces an exclude whack-a-mole with a positive shape, measured to keep all 40 real sea-salt rows (sidecar sea_salt_routing_after) and drop 26 snack/candy names. The cross-commodity class (flavour phrases) has no single library today; category-excludes.json is a food-CLASS library (beverage/pet/household) and cannot express 'a snack named after its seasoning'. Not proposed this round; the measured leftovers (4 seed packets on kale/onions/lettuce) are listed in the sidecar as follow-ups.

items.subject: Daily chain re-anchors 584 authored specs and does not commit them
evidence: PREMISE VERIFIED against the tree: git log shows 91f895ef 08:24:50 'Daily pipeline: refresh prices + feed (2026-09-02) [daily]' (message from capture-run.ps1 line 802) touching grocery/out (41+10+4 files), grocery (9), graph/identity (16), public (4), meal-prep (3: the servedPaths trio) and NONE of the specs; then 26c2b0e0 08:29:18 'meal-prep: the 2026-09-02 daily re-anchor and surface rebuild, committed as its own change' = 536 files, 1066 insertions / 1066 deletions: 530 meal-prep/db/recipes/*.json + meal-prep/cheapnow-data.js, dinner-data.js, stretcher-data.js + site/tools/cheap-dinners-tool.html, dinner-tonight-tool.html, payday-stretcher-tool.html. git status --porcelain on meal-prep/db/recipes now: 0 dirty.

WHY THE CHAIN'S COMMIT CANNOT INCLUDE ITS OWN OUTPUT: capture-run.ps1 line 647 stages inputPaths + (if shipServed) servedPaths; servedPaths (lines 625-630) = public, meal-prep/db/costed.json, meal-prep/db/cost-flags.txt, meal-prep/pipeline/v2-perserving.json, v2-perserving.prev.json, v2-inversions.json, meal-prep/free-rotation.json, meal-prep/ingredient-map.json, meal-prep/recipes-db.json. The seven paths reanchor-all + build-cards rewrite (check-ad-cycles.ps1 lines 751-790, gated on cv2Ok) are on neither list.

shipServed = runDownstream and verdictSeen and not guardsBlocked (line 641), read from out\chain-verdict.json that check-ad-cycles writes after guards (line 947-949): the served set only ships on a green verdict, which is the right rule for spec output too.

surface_fix.what: the chain's own commit stages the seven paths it rewrites, under its own [daily] label
surface_fix.exact_change: servedPaths += 'meal-prep/db/recipes', 'meal-prep/cheapnow-data.js', 'meal-prep/dinner-data.js', 'meal-prep/stretcher-data.js', 'site/tools/cheap-dinners-tool.html', 'site/tools/dinner-tonight-tool.html', 'site/tools/payday-stretcher-tool.html' (served set: staged only with a green chain-verdict, exactly like recipes-db.json, so a guards-blocked day never ships re-anchored prose from a rejected board; on such a day the existing 'guards-blocked' failure already pages and the specs stay dirty on purpose).

items.root_cause: The staging list is an enumeration written before the close-the-loop stage existed (2026-08-07); every artifact added to the chain since then had to be remembered here by hand, and the re-anchor's outputs never were. Class: checkpoint-before-durable's sibling - a commit step that does not know what its own run wrote. The push-data-sweeps-your-edit risk is the consequence: 536 authored files sit dirty on a shared tree until some other session's blanket add takes them.

root_fix.what: a guard that fails the run when the chain leaves its own tracked output dirty after its commit
root_fix.exact_change: after the commit step, when shipServed and the check-ad-cycles output for this run contained 'REANCHOR-COMPLETE': run git status --porcelain on the seven paths; if any line: failed += 'reanchor-uncommitted', Write-Output the count and first 10 paths, Send-Alert 'Daily chain left re-anchored specs uncommitted'. Test in test-commit-size-gate.ps1's synthetic repo.

evidence: The one signal: recentVerified = rows whose as_of is within 48h (pull-regular-familyfare.ps1 1038-1041) = 163, threshold 500 (line 156). ff-term-ledger.json (10:33): terms last bought 09-02: 21, 09-01: 14, 08-31: 3, 08-30: 34, 08-24..08-29: 7 per day, 08-23: 95. Get-ScheduledTask: only 'TC Grocery Ad Pulls 0700', 'TC Grocery Daily Capture 0800', 'TC Grocery Capture Watchdog 0930' exist - there is NO 3-hourly Family Fare task (capture-run.ps1 lines 462-476 record the same finding on 2026-09-01, queue 056e6b, and ship 'shard window 1 of 3' piggybacked on the existing tasks). The design budget is 7 terms per window (capture policy, line 686: 'the main pass stops at TermBudget (7 today)'), so one window per day = 7 terms per day = an 85-day rotation of 598 terms; three windows = 21 per day, which is exactly what today's ledger shows (21). Measurement (C) 'the catalog is gaining' is the 90-day carry-forward union, not verification: a catalog cannot shrink until rows age past 90 days, so it is not evidence against this alert.

Tolerance vs period, answered: 500 rows per 48h was calibrated when a run bought 60-90 terms; under 3 windows x 7 terms x up to 25 rows the 48h ceiling is about 1,050, so the floor is sound but tight - any two throttled windows in a 48h span will page. The alert fired on the trailing window (08-31: 3 terms, 09-01: 14) before the 09-01 fix had a full day.
items.root_cause: Cadence, not pacing and not a threshold bug: the sharded sweep was designed for several windows a day and only one ever existed (the 08:00 task), fixed 2026-09-01 by riding the 07:00 and 09:30 tasks. The alert measured the last 48h before that fix took hold.
items.resolution_note: No code change here: the 09-01 shard-window fix (capture-run.ps1 462-480, queue 056e6b) is already lifting term buys (7 per day -> 21 today).
